status: draft for G1: Cowork's seed hypotheses plus questions drawn from real alert conditions and use cases. Expected homes are hypotheses until the D16 amendment rules on them; nothing here is ratified.
rules: Plan section 5.1. Each question is a person's problem and never names a topic or an element. expected_element is an id from elements.json, or `no data yet` when the platform does not capture the thing today (so a miss is routed to implementation, not blamed on the taxonomy). ruled marks a placement settled by a ruling recorded in rulings.json (R3, R4, Nate, 2026-10-17); expected_topic is the ruled home, and a ruling is applied at analysis time, never by editing a run log. edge_tags are listed in edge-tests.draft.md. `source` is one of ask_log, alert_history, family, synthetic; note says what a question was drawn from.

questions.problem: Is it too humid in the cabin?
questions.start_context: Monitoring screen for the cabin. Kitchen humidity reads 68 percent, the mechanical room 55 percent.
questions.note: Seed from the plan; humidity feeds a stale-air judgment but is a moisture reading.

questions.problem: The cabin feels freezing. How cold is it inside, and how cold is it outside?
questions.start_context: Monitoring screen for the cabin. The kitchen sensor reads 9 C; the outdoor probe reads -14 C.
questions.note: Pairs with the `cold` need in concepts.json.

questions.problem: Will the pipes in the mechanical room freeze tonight?
questions.start_context: Monitoring screen for the cabin. The mechanical room reads 4 C and the heater plug is on; outside is -18 C.
questions.note: Drawn from the freeze-risk condition the workflow engine already knows.

questions.problem: It feels stuffy in here. Is the air actually stale?
questions.start_context: Monitoring screen for the cabin. The Kidde monitor is online; every reading is inside its normal range.
questions.note: Pairs with the `stuffy` need; the Kidde monitor is the one live air-quality source.

questions.problem: Is the carbon monoxide level okay?
questions.start_context: Monitoring screen for the cabin. The Kidde monitor is online and reports no alarm.
questions.note: Ruled (Nate, 2026-10-17, R4 option B): the reading stays with its measurement's topic; the alarm state surfaces only through alerts and never feeds a badge.

questions.problem: Is the air in the main-floor bedroom stale?
questions.start_context: Monitoring screen for the cabin. No air-quality sensor has been installed in the bedroom yet.
questions.note: The SEN66 nodes of Doc 27 are ordered, not commissioned.

questions.problem: Is smoke from the wood stove getting into the downstairs air?
questions.start_context: Monitoring screen for the cabin. No particle sensor is installed.
questions.note: Particles are in the ontology (Doc 27) but nothing captures them today.

questions.problem: Is anyone at the cabin right now?
questions.start_context: Home screen, signed in from Minneapolis. The entry motion sensor fired four minutes ago; nobody has reported arriving.
questions.note: Seed from the plan.

questions.problem: Did someone leave the front door open?
questions.start_context: Home screen. The front door contact sensor reads open and has for 20 minutes.
questions.note: Drawn from the door-open condition.

questions.problem: Is the front door locked?
questions.start_context: Home screen. No lock is registered for the cabin.
questions.note: Candidate grouping Access & Perimeter: the probe decides whether locks and gates earn their own topic.

questions.problem: Is there water on the floor anywhere?
questions.start_context: Home screen. All four leak sensors report dry.
questions.note: Ruled (R4 option B): D16 keeps water_leak under security_presence; the alarm state surfaces only through alerts and never feeds a badge.

questions.problem: Is the mechanical room heater drawing power right now?
questions.start_context: Monitoring screen for the cabin. The heater plug is switched on.
questions.note: The real smart plug reports power.

questions.problem: Did the power go out while we were away?
questions.start_context: Home screen, signed in from Minneapolis. The hub has been up for 40 days.
questions.note: Nothing detects loss of mains power today (UC-16 notes a later continuity step).

questions.problem: Can I run the dryer right now without tripping the breaker?
questions.start_context: Home screen. No whole-house power monitor is registered.
questions.note: Candidate wording for Energy from the plan.

questions.problem: Which sensors are about to die?
questions.start_context: Device list. Several battery sensors are paired; two report under 15 percent.
questions.note: Seed from the plan.

questions.problem: The mechanical room leak sensor has not reported in a day. Is it broken?
questions.start_context: Device list. That sensor's last check-in was 26 hours ago; the others reported minutes ago.
questions.note: Drawn from the stale-device condition.

questions.problem: The kitchen sensor is slow to update. Is it too far from the hub?
questions.start_context: Device list. The kitchen sensor reports every few minutes; its signal strength is low and falling.
questions.note: Signal quality of one device to its hub.

questions.problem: Is the backup battery in the power unit getting low?
questions.start_context: Home screen. No backup power unit is registered.
questions.note: Ruled (Nate, 2026-10-17, R3): a house or backup-unit battery belongs to Device Health.

questions.problem: The internet is slow. Where do I look?
questions.start_context: Home screen at the cabin. Video calls stutter; all devices show online.
questions.note: Seed from the plan. The Starlink terminal is an ontology element (hw_starlink_terminal) but no measurement is captured.

questions.problem: Why do six devices show offline at once?
questions.start_context: Device list. Six sensors went offline within the same minute; the hub itself is up.
questions.note: Seed from the plan: more than one device loses something at once.

questions.problem: Is my phone online?
questions.start_context: Home screen. The phone last reported to Home Assistant three hours ago.
questions.note: Seed from the plan. A phone's presence signal is not its reachability.

questions.problem: Can I still reach the cabin from here?
questions.start_context: Home screen, signed in from Minneapolis. The page loaded a minute ago and data looks old.
questions.note: Drawn from UC-16 (knowing the cabin has gone offline).

questions.problem: What alerts fired last night?
questions.start_context: Rules and alerts screen. Three alerts fired between midnight and six.
questions.note: Seed from the plan.

questions.problem: Has the freeze alarm ever gone off this winter?
questions.start_context: Rules and alerts screen. The mechanical room hit 2 C once in November.
questions.note: A question about past events, not today's temperature.

questions.problem: Which door alert keeps firing?
questions.start_context: Rules and alerts screen. The second door contact has alerted nine times this week.
questions.note: Repeated alerts from one device across time.

questions.problem: Was the cabin busy this weekend?
questions.start_context: Home screen. Motion and door sensors have been reporting all weekend.
questions.note: The Occupancy view is not built (its tab is marked coming soon).

questions.problem: How many times did someone come through the entry this week?
questions.start_context: Home screen. The entry motion sensor has fired many times.
questions.note: A count over time is a view; the raw motion signal feeds it.

questions.problem: Is the cabin usually empty on weekdays?
questions.start_context: Home screen. Several months of motion history exist.
questions.note: A pattern over months, which the unbuilt Occupancy view would summarize.

questions.problem: Why did the lights just dim?
questions.start_context: Home screen at the cabin. The lights dimmed for two seconds and recovered; the heater plug is on.
questions.note: Candidate computed view from the plan: the probe decides whether it earns one.
